pr_title: fix(ivy): support dynamic query tokens in AOT mode
pr_body:
For view and content queries, the Ivy compiler attempts to statically
evaluate the predicate token so that string predicates containing
comma-separated reference names can be split into an array of strings
during compilation. When the predicate is a dynamic value that cannot be
statically interpreted at compile time, the compiler would previously
produce an error. This behavior breaks a use-case where an `InjectionToken`
is being used as query predicate, as the usage of the `new` keyword
prevents such predicates from being statically evaluated.

This commit changes the behavior to no longer produce an error for
dynamic values. Instead, the expression is emitted as is into the
generated code, postponing the evaluation to happen at runtime.

Fixes #34267
Resolves FW-1828
pr_comments: This change raises the question: should the typings in `@angular/core` be adjusted to properly accept `InjectionToken`. including acceptance tests to validate this use-case is supported at runtime?
Thanks for fixing this, my library broke on Angular 9 due to this issue :(

issue_context.title: @ViewChild(MyInjectorToken as any, { static: false }) no longer works with Ivy
issue_context.body:
# 🐞 bug report ### Affected Package Ivy Compiler ### Is this a regression? Yes. This used to work with Angular 8 ### Description To get view children or content children that implement a certain abstract class or interface requires a bit of a workaround - casting the injector token to "any" - but was definitely supported in so far that somebody had to have written the code that deals with the injector token. For details, see the related issues: * https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/12758 * https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/21152 With a new Angular 9 (9.0.0-rc.5) project, the same mechanism fails in the AOT compillation step with the message: "error TS-991010: @ViewChild predicate cannot be interpreted" ## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-viewchildtoken-angular8-4dpwkt?file=src%2Fapp%2Fhello.component.ts 1. Download the Stackblitz sample 2. Upgrade the project to Angular 9 rc5 with `ng update --next=true @angular/cli @angular/core` 3. Build the project in AOT mode ## 🔥 Exception or Error 

error TS-991010: @ViewChild predicate cannot be interpreted
## 🌍 Your Environment **Angular Version:** 

Angular CLI: 9.0.0-rc.5
Node: 10.16.0
OS: win32 x64

Angular: 9.0.0-rc.5
... animations, cli, common, compiler, compiler-cli, core, forms
... language-service, platform-browser, platform-browser-dynamic
... router
Ivy Workspace: Yes

*Edit*: A fellow developer had some trouble to reproduce the issue, so think it's worth mention that the error only appears when building in AOT mode.
comments:
Interesting bug, and thank you for the clear reproduction! This is indeed an issue.

What's going on here is that Angular sees `const ComponentInterfaceToken = new InjectionToken<...>(...)` and realizes that it cannot statically determine the value as it involves the `new` operation. The compiler is trying to verify that the value in question is either a string or a `class` instance as specified by the type of `@ViewChild()`.

This is why you need a cast here - you're going beyond Angular's public API when you pass an `InjectionToken` as the query predicate. The fact that this worked in the runtime is an implementation detail.

Will that be fixed by Ivy stable? I use that a lot, it is very helpful :( My latest usecase — I have directives for Web Audio API. They all extend native AudioNodes and provide themselves as AUDIO_NODE token. I need to be able to query all nodes in the view/content.
